definitions.gloss: warding off evil; exorcism; purification from bad luck
definitions.explanation: A ritual or act performed to drive away bad luck or evil spirits, typically at a shrine or temple. Commonly done during unlucky years (厄年) or after a series of misfortunes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{厄払|やくばら}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I had a purification ritual done at a shrine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厄年|やくどし}→厄年：05809_yakudoshi⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{厄払|やくばら}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧だ。
examples.english: This year is an unlucky year, so I plan to go for a purification ritual.

examples.japanese: ⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いた→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{厄払|やくばら}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祈祷|きとう}→祈祷：22031_kitou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧ことにした。
examples.english: Since bad things kept happening, our whole family decided to receive a purification prayer.

notes:
A traditional Japanese practice of seeking spiritual purification, most commonly performed at Shinto shrines. It is especially common during ⟦{厄年|やくどし}→厄年：05809_yakudoshi⟧ (unlucky years), which are specific ages believed to bring misfortune (e.g., 25 and 42 for men, 19 and 33 for women).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厄払|やくばら}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to have a purification done
- {厄払|やくばら}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祈祷|きとう}→祈祷：22031_kitou⟧: purification prayer
- {厄払|やくばら}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go for purification

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many Japanese visit shrines at the start of the new year or around ⟦{節分|せつぶん}→節分：18971_setsubun⟧ (early February) for {厄払|やくばら}い. The ⟦{豆|まめ}まき→豆まき：14275_mamemaki⟧ (bean-throwing) ceremony at ⟦{節分|せつぶん}→節分：18971_setsubun⟧ is itself a form of {厄払|やくばら}い.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦お{祓|はら}い→お祓い：15835_oharai⟧: purification ritual — broader term, not limited to bad luck
- ⟦{厄除|やくよ}け→厄除け：24744_yakuyoke⟧: protection against evil — focuses on prevention rather than removal
